serverForm.localHint: Local pseudo-server — commands run directly on this machine, no SSH connection. Only notes and tags are editable.
serverForm.ed25519Recommendation: Recommended: Ed25519 key. Generate a new one with `ssh-keygen -t ed25519`. RSA keys keep working.
serverForm.agentHint: Uses the locally running SSH agent, no further details needed.

identityFile.looksValid: Looks like a valid OpenSSH key.
identityFile.permissionsTooOpen: The file's permissions are too open (readable or writable by group or others). Connecting will be refused until the permissions are tightened — e.g. fix it with "chmod 600" on the file.
identityFile.permissionsOk: The file's permissions are tight enough.
identityFile.encrypted: The key is encrypted — the stored passphrase is required to connect.
identityFile.checkFailed: The pre-check could not be requested. This does not block saving — the file is checked again when connecting.

convertToKeychain.hint: Copies the key file's content into the encrypted database once and switches the auth method to "Private Key". Protects against a file with permissions that are too open, or a directory someone else can read.
convertToKeychain.checkFailed: The pre-check could not be requested, so the button stays disabled. Try again, e.g. by switching to another server and back.
convertToKeychain.confirmWhatChanges: The login will then depend on the encrypted database, no longer on this file.
convertToKeychain.confirmWhatStays: The file stays unchanged on disk — it is neither deleted nor modified:

serverForm.sudoHint: Automatically fed via standard input for a "sudo" command suggested by the AI — never stored on the target server.
serverForm.sudoUnchangedUnknown: (empty = unchanged; without access to the encrypted database it cannot be determined whether one is stored)
serverForm.deletedWithLeftoverSecretsTitle: Server deleted — secrets remain in the database
serverForm.deletedWithLeftoverSecretsHint: The server is gone, but at least one secret could not be removed from the encrypted database. It is now orphaned (the server no longer exists). The exact cause is in the log:
serverForm.removeSudoPasswordFailed: The sudo password could not be removed — it is still in the encrypted database and will be fed in again on the next "sudo".
serverForm.postIngestHint: Controls whether and when extra confirmation is required after server content (command output, files, notes) has been read during this session. Regardless of this setting, such content is always clearly marked as data, never treated as an instruction.

strict.label: Strict
strict.description: Once server content has been read during the session, every further action requires confirmation.

balanced.label: Balanced
balanced.description: Only actions that change something require extra confirmation afterward; plain read actions keep following the existing rules. Selected automatically for new servers.

standard.label: Standard
standard.description: No extra confirmation after reading — only the existing rules apply.

serverForm.aiInjectionCheckLabel: Have freshly read server content checked by AI for possible injected instructions
serverForm.aiInjectionCheckHint: Uses the AI provider configured under "Risk Second Opinion" for an extra assessment before a follow-up action runs automatically. This check is itself only an AI assessment, not reliable detection — a deliberately crafted attempt can fool it. A suspected match triggers a confirmation prompt; no suspicion leaves the other rules unchanged.
serverForm.aiInjectionCheckUnavailableHint: Requires a configured risk second opinion (Settings → Risk Second Opinion) — without a provider, this option has no effect.
serverForm.deleteNoKeychainImpact: No secrets in the database, no other servers affected.
serverForm.secretWillBeDeleted: Will be removed from the database: {{label}}
serverForm.secretMayBeDeleted: Could not be checked (database not readable), will be removed if possible: {{label}}
serverForm.identityFilePassphraseMayBeDeleted: If a passphrase is stored for this key file, it will be removed as well. The key file itself stays untouched on disk — it is never in the database.
serverForm.serverWillLoseJumpHost: Loses the jump-host reference to this server: {{name}}
serverForm.deleteAlwaysRemovesHistory: This also permanently deletes this server's chat history, notes, and tags.

testResult.authFailed: ✗ Login rejected. Check the user name and password or key.
testResult.timeout: ✗ The server isn't responding. Check address, port and firewall.

serverForm.largeNoteHint: This note is very large and may be shortened for the AI context during long sessions. The stored note stays fully intact.
serverForm.sftpServerPathHint: Only needed if automatic detection fails for the file browser with elevated rights, e.g. /usr/lib/openssh/sftp-server. Leave empty = automatic.
serverForm.startDirectoryHint: Absolute path (/…) or a path starting with ~/. The terminal changes there with a visible cd, the file browser opens there. AI commands always run in the home directory. Leave empty = home directory.

startDirectoryInvalid.controlCharacter: The start directory must not contain control characters.

actionCard.commandCancelledNotice: ⚠ Manually cancelled — output may be incomplete, no regular exit code.

hostKeyDialog.mismatchHeading: This server's key is no longer the same.
hostKeyDialog.mismatchBodyAfterHost: is presenting a different key than the one stored last time. This can indicate a man-in-the-middle attack. Only continue if you are sure the server key changed legitimately (e.g. server reinstallation).
hostKeyDialog.unknownBodyAfterHost: for the first time. Please check the fingerprint before trusting it.

mcp.tabHint: Session of an external tool (MCP) — its own connection, separate from your sessions.
mcp.readOnlyHint: This session belongs to an external tool (MCP). It only shows the tool's actions to confirm or reject and their results; there is no chat input or terminal here. Closing it ends the MCP session and rejects pending confirmations.

sessionTabs.confirmClosePending: A confirmation is still pending for "{{name}}". Close the tab anyway? The pending action will then count as rejected.

aiProvider.title: AI Provider
aiProvider.openLogs: Open diagnostic logs in file manager
aiProvider.apiKeyFormatHint: Doesn't look like a {{providerLabel}} key – expected a prefix like "{{expectedPrefix}}". You can still save it; providers change formats occasionally.
aiProvider.testResultAuthFailed: ✗ Authentication failed – check the API key
aiProvider.testResultRateLimited: Credentials look valid, but the provider is rate-limiting right now. Test again in a minute.
aiProvider.modelDiscoveryFailedHint: Could not load models automatically — enter the model name manually.
aiProvider.extraHeadersHint: Attached to every request to this provider (e.g. OpenRouter's HTTP-Referer/X-Title).
aiProvider.maxTokensOverrideHint: Only for this provider, only for the main chat. Leave empty for the automatic, model-aware value — only change it for a self-hosted/gateway model with an unknown output maximum.
aiProvider.maxTokensOverrideMustBePositive: Max. response length must be greater than 0
aiProvider.attestationDisclaimerBeforeNot: This value is fetched unmodified from the provider and is
aiProvider.attestationDisclaimerAfterNot: cryptographically verified by Smart SSH. To verify independently, use the verification tool provided by the hardware/provider.
aiProvider.riskClassifierHint: Optional: a second AI provider assesses, in addition to the rule-based check, whether a command might contain sensitive data. A locally running model (e.g. via Ollama) is recommended, so this second opinion doesn't necessarily go to an external provider either.
aiProvider.redRiskAlwaysConfirmHint: When this is on, any suggestion rated red on either risk axis always requires confirmation – even against an Allow rule. Independent of whether the AI second opinion above is enabled. A change only takes effect from the next connection onward.
aiProvider.ollamaProbeFoundHeading: Ollama is running on this machine.
aiProvider.ollamaProbeFoundHintWillActivate: Will be used as the active provider.
aiProvider.ollamaProbeFoundHintInactive: Will be added as another provider (another one stays active for now).
aiProvider.addHintWillActivate: Will be used as the active provider, since none is active yet.
aiProvider.ollamaProbeEmptyHeading: Ollama is running, but no model is loaded yet.
aiProvider.ollamaProbePullHint: Load a model: run `ollama pull <model>` in a terminal, then search again.
aiProvider.ollamaProbeNotFoundInstructions: Install Ollama from ollama.com, start it and load a model (e.g. `ollama pull llama3`), then search again.
aiProvider.webResearch: Web research (search and read web pages)
aiProvider.webResearchHint: The AI may search the web and read web pages (text only) while answering. The provider fetches the pages; this computer opens no additional connection. Applies to sessions connected after the change.

errors.SSH_CONNECTION_FAILED: Connection failed – is the host reachable (address, port, network)?
errors.SSH_AUTH_FAILED: Login rejected. Check the user name and password or key in the server settings.
errors.SSH_TIMEOUT: The server isn't responding. Check address, port and firewall, then connect again.
errors.SSH_CONNECTION_REFUSED: The server refused the connection. Check the port and whether an SSH service is running there.
errors.SSH_HOST_NOT_FOUND: Unknown host name. Check the address spelling (or enter the IP address).
errors.SSH_HOST_UNREACHABLE: The server can't be reached from this network. Check your network/VPN.
errors.SSH_CONNECTION_CLOSED: The server closed the connection during setup. Check that an SSH service runs on this port; wait a moment if too many attempts were made.
errors.SSH_SESSION_CLOSED: The connection to the server was lost. Reconnect to continue.
errors.SSH_HOST_KEY_NOT_TRUSTED: Connection cancelled because the host key wasn't confirmed. If you trust the server, connect again and verify the fingerprint.
errors.SSH_HOST_KEY_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT: The host key prompt wasn't answered in time; the key was not trusted. Connect again.
errors.SSH_CONNECTION_ABANDONED: Connection attempt cancelled (e.g. the app reloaded while the host key prompt was open). Connect again.
errors.AI_AUTH_FAILED: Authentication with the AI provider failed – check the API key
errors.AI_RATE_LIMITED: The AI provider is currently throttling requests (rate limit) – the app already retried automatically a few times. Please wait a moment and send the message again.
errors.AI_NETWORK_ERROR: Can't reach the AI provider. Check your internet connection and, for a custom endpoint, the base URL, then send again.
errors.AI_INVALID_RESPONSE: Unexpected response from the AI provider
errors.AI_CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE: Context too large for the AI provider. Lower "Max. response length (tokens)" or start a new chat.
errors.AI_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE: The AI provider reported an error (e.g. maintenance or overload). Try again later; if it persists, check the provider settings.
errors.AI_RESPONSE_TRUNCATED: The AI response was too long for a complete command
errors.AI_MODEL_NOT_FOUND: The AI provider doesn't know this model. Check the model name in Settings ("Load models" lists the available ones); for Ollama, pull it first with `ollama pull <name>`.
errors.AI_LOCAL_PROVIDER_UNREACHABLE: The local AI service isn't responding. Start Ollama (or your local server) and try again.
errors.AI_TIMEOUT: The AI provider took too long to respond. Wait a moment and send again; with a local model, check whether the machine is busy or the model too large.
errors.AI_WEB_RESEARCH_REJECTED: The AI provider rejects web research for this account. Turn off “Web research” for this provider under “AI Provider” in the settings.
errors.AI_NO_ACTIVE_PROVIDER: No active AI provider yet. Add one under Settings → AI provider and set it active.
errors.FILTER_PARSE_AMBIGUOUS: Command could not be parsed unambiguously
errors.FILTER_SUBSTITUTION_TOO_DEEP: Command nested too deeply to be safely analyzed
errors.FILTER_RULE_PATTERN_INVALID: Invalid pattern in a filter rule. Please correct the pattern.
errors.FILTER_POST_INGEST_REQUIRES_CONFIRM: Server content was already read during this session – requires confirmation
errors.FILTER_INJECTION_SUSPECTED_REQUIRES_CONF: Possible attempt to inject instructions via server content detected – requires confirmation
errors.FILTER_MCP_ORIGIN_REQUIRES_CONFIRM: Requested via MCP – always requires confirmation
errors.FILTER_SUDO_PASSWORD_REQUIRES_CONFIRM: Uses the stored sudo password – always requires confirmation
errors.FILTER_SECRET_PATH_READ_REQUIRES_CONFIRM: Reads a file with credentials (e.g. SSH key, .env, /etc/shadow) – always requires confirmation
errors.FILTER_EARLIER_ACTION_REJECTED_REQUIRES_: An earlier action in this response was rejected – requires confirmation
errors.FILTER_SFTP_SERVER_REQUIRES_CONFIRM: Starts sftp-server (with sudo: file access with root privileges) – always requires confirmation
errors.FILTER_COMMAND_NOT_ASSESSABLE_REQUIRES_C: Command is too long or too deeply nested to be checked – always requires confirmation
errors.FILTER_RED_RISK_REQUIRES_CONFIRM: Risk assessed as red, or could not be assessed reliably (e.g. too long) – always requires confirmation
errors.GROUP_SELF_PARENT: A group cannot be its own parent group
errors.GROUP_CYCLE_DETECTED: Cycle: the selected parent group is a subgroup of this group
errors.SERVER_JUMP_HOST_LOCAL: The local pseudo-server cannot be used as a jump host
errors.KEY_FILE_NOT_FOUND: The key file was not found at the given path.
errors.KEY_FILE_NOT_READABLE: The key file cannot be read with the current permissions.
errors.KEY_FILE_PERMISSIONS_TOO_OPEN: The key file is readable or writable by group or others — like ssh, this rejects the login. Fix it with "chmod 600" on the file.
errors.KEY_FILE_TOO_LARGE: The key file exceeds the allowed size of 1 MiB.
errors.KEY_FILE_NOT_A_REGULAR_FILE: The given path is not a regular file (e.g. a directory or a device).
errors.KEY_FILE_PATH_NOT_ABSOLUTE: The path must be absolute (no relative path, no "~user").
errors.KEY_FILE_INVALID_KEY: The file's content is not a valid OpenSSH key.
errors.SERVER_IDENTITY_FILE_REQUIRED: Path to the key file is required
errors.SERVER_NOT_AN_IDENTITY_FILE: This server does not log in with a key file
errors.IDENTITY_FILE_ROLLBACK_LEFT_KEY_BEHIND: The key was already written to the encrypted database but could not be removed again after a failure — the entry stayed behind. The exact cause is in the log.
errors.FIRST_RUN_NOTICE_NOT_ACKNOWLEDGED: The first-run notice must be acknowledged first
errors.KEYCHAIN_UNAVAILABLE: The system keyring is unavailable — this does not affect your secrets: API keys, server passwords, passphrases, and sudo passwords live in the encrypted database. The diagnostics view in the settings shows the exact reason and the next step.
errors.KEYCHAIN_ACCESS_FAILED: Access to the system keyring failed. It may be locked, or access was denied. Please try again — the exact reason is in the log.
errors.SECRET_STORE_FAILED: Access to a stored secret (e.g. API key, server password, passphrase, sudo password, or token) in the encrypted database failed — for example because the database is not writable or out of space. Nothing was changed; the exact cause is in the log.
errors.WRONG_MASTER_PASSWORD: Wrong password, or the file is damaged. The two cannot be told apart from the outside. Nothing was changed.
errors.MASTER_PASSWORD_FILE_FAILED: The key to your database could not be read or written just now. Nothing was changed; the cause is in the log.
errors.MASTER_PASSWORD_FILE_ABSENT: There is no key file at this location anymore — Smart SSH now runs this database in keychain mode. Nothing was changed. Try again.
errors.MASTER_PASSWORD_REJECTED: The master password was rejected: at least 12 characters, and both entries must match.
errors.STARTUP_FAILED: The startup did not complete. Nothing was changed; the log names the cause.
errors.KEYCHAIN_HOLDS_ANOTHER_KEY: The keychain holds a different key. Nothing was changed — confirm the replacement if that is what you want.
errors.APP_LOCKED: Smart SSH is still locked. Unlock it with your master password first.
errors.MASTER_PASSWORD_MODE_MISMATCH: This operation does not match where the key is currently kept. Nothing was changed — reopen the settings, they show the active mode.
errors.MASTER_PASSWORD_WARNING_NOT_CONFIRMED: The master password warning has not been confirmed. Without that password all data is lost and there is no recovery — tick the box and set it up again. Nothing was changed.
errors.KEYCHAIN_KEY_MISMATCH: The key in the keychain does not belong to this database. Nothing was changed — storing it would make the database unreadable at the next startup.

mcpServer.hint: External MCP clients can use this to propose commands, file reads/writes, and note updates on allow-listed servers — every request always requires confirmation in the app, regardless of existing allow rules.
mcpServer.regenerateConfirm: Generate a new token? The old token becomes invalid immediately — already configured external clients must be updated with the new value.
mcpServer.confirmTimeoutHint: How long a waiting external tool call gets a response before the app decides — the confirmation request itself stays open in the app either way. Applies the next time the server (re)starts; a running server restarts immediately when you change this.
mcpServer.exampleConfigHint: Example configuration for Claude Code (.mcp.json / "claude mcp add --transport http"):

firstRunNotice.title: Before you start
firstRunNotice.responsibilityText: Smart SSH proposes commands generated by an AI based on your requests. Nothing runs without your confirmation — unless you've explicitly set up a rule that allows it. You're responsible for every command you approve.
firstRunNotice.encryptionText: The local database is encrypted. Your operating system's keychain holds the key — or, if you set one up, your master password does. Anyone with access to your unlocked user account can read the data.

chatSessionPicker.deleteConfirm: Delete this conversation permanently? This cannot be undone.

chatRetention.label: Keep chat history for
chatRetention.hint: Automatically deletes ended conversations older than this. Active conversations are never affected.

fileElevation.toggleTitle: Open the file browser with elevated rights (sudo) — requires a passwordless sudo rule for sftp-server
fileElevation.banner: Elevated rights active: all file actions in this browser run as {{user}}.
fileElevation.sudoersIntro: Elevated mode needs a sudo rule without password for sftp-server on the server. This line matches this server and login:
fileElevation.sudoersHowTo: Add it on the server, e.g. with “sudo visudo -f /etc/sudoers.d/smart-ssh-sftp”.
fileElevation.sudoersWarning: Important: this rule gives the SSH login passwordless file access as {{user}} — not only for this browser but for everything running under this login, including commands suggested by the AI. Anyone with the SSH key can read and write every file; write access as root is practically full root access. Decide deliberately.

failure.unsupported: The local server has no elevated mode.

startup.stateUnknown: Smart SSH could not read its startup state. Nothing was changed. Try again; if it persists, the log names the cause.
startup.unlockIntro: Your local database is encrypted with a master password. Enter it to unlock Smart SSH.
startup.failedAttempts: Failed attempts in this program run so far: {{attempts}}.
startup.wayOutHint: You can start over if you no longer know your master password. Your existing data is lost in the process — the files are only renamed, not deleted. You will be asked once more before anything happens.
startup.unusableWrapping: The key file next to your database is unusable: its format or parameters are wrong, and no password can open it any more. You can start over — your existing data is lost in the process, the files are only renamed.
startup.unreachableWrapping: The key file next to your database is in its place but cannot be read right now — perhaps another program is holding it open, or the permissions are wrong. Nothing was changed. This says nothing about its contents: fix the cause and try again.
startup.passwordsDiffer: The two entries do not match.
startup.noRecoveryWarning: I understand: without this password all data is lost. There is no recovery.

masterPassword.modeHeading: Where the key to your database is kept
masterPassword.modePassword: In a key file next to the database, protected by your master password. Smart SSH asks for it at startup.
masterPassword.modeKeychain: In your operating system's keychain. Smart SSH starts without asking.
masterPassword.setUpIntro: Afterwards Smart SSH asks for this password at startup, and the key leaves your operating system's keychain.
masterPassword.passwordsDiffer: The two entries do not match.
masterPassword.noRecoveryWarning: I understand: without this password all data is lost. There is no recovery.
masterPassword.setUpDone: The master password is set up. Smart SSH will ask for it at the next startup.
masterPassword.changeDone: The master password has been changed.
masterPassword.switchIntro: The key moves into your operating system's keychain; the key file is removed afterwards. Smart SSH then starts without asking.
masterPassword.switchedToKeychain: The key is now kept in your operating system's keychain.
masterPassword.anotherKeyTitle: The keychain holds a different key
masterPassword.anotherKeyText: The keychain holds a different key. Backups encrypted with that key will become unreadable. Replace it?
